It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} (major shrine), and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine rank}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

It is also commonly known as “Iruka-no-miya.” The shrine is known as being associated with the ancient powerful clan, the {{ill|Soga clan|ar|سوغا (عشيرة)|ca|Clan Soga|de|Soga (Klan)|es|Clan Soga|fa|خاندان سوگا|fi|Soga-klaani|fr|Clan Soga|hr|Soga (klan)|hu|Szoga klán|id|Klan Soga|it|Clan Soga|ja|蘇我氏|ko|소가씨|nl|Soga|pl|Soga (ród)|pt|Clã Soga|ru|Сога (род)|sh|Soga (klan)|tr|Soga boyu|uk|Рід Соґа|vi|Gia tộc Soga|zh|蘇我氏|qid=Q909854}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
The enshrined deities are the following two {{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}:
:* '''Sogatsuhiko-no-Kami''' (そがつひこのかみ, also written 宗我都比古神)
:* '''Sogatsuhime-no-Kami''' (そがつひめのかみ, also written 宗我都比売神)

In the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed as having two seats of deities. The entry records the name as “Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine,” meaning “the shrine that enshrines Sogatsuhiko in Soga (= Soga/Soga/Soga: a place name).” One of the two seats is identified as Sogatsuhiko-no-Kami, but the identity of the other seat is unclear.

Because the shrine name and deity name include “Sogatsuhiko,” the ritual practices of Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine are thought to be connected to the ancient powerful {{ill|Soga clan|ar|سوغا (عشيرة)|ca|Clan Soga|de|Soga (Klan)|es|Clan Soga|fa|خاندان سوگا|fi|Soga-klaani|fr|Clan Soga|hr|Soga (klan)|hu|Szoga klán|id|Klan Soga|it|Clan Soga|ja|蘇我氏|ko|소가씨|nl|Soga|pl|Soga (ród)|pt|Clã Soga|ru|Сога (род)|sh|Soga (klan)|tr|Soga boyu|uk|Рід Соґа|vi|Gia tộc Soga|zh|蘇我氏|qid=Q909854}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}. Although the Soga clan is a well-known lineage, its original homeland ({{ill|Korean clans|es|Bon-gwan|fr|Système de Pon'gwan|it|Bongwan|ja|本貫|ko|본관|ms|Bon-gwan|pl|Koreańskie klany|ro|Bon-gwan|ru|Пон (корейский клан)|zh|本貫|qid=Q846706}}) has not been definitively identified. Three main theories are known: that it was located in Soga (the area around present-day Soga-chō, Kashihara City) in {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi In all cases, these figures are regarded as distant ancestors of the Soga clan. In contrast, the present practice enshrines the two deities Sogatsuhiko and Sogatsuhime, with their two wooden statues worshipped as the {{ill|Shintai|de|Shintai|el|Σίνταϊ|es|Shintai|fa|شین‌تای|fi|Shintai|fr|Shintai|hr|Shintai|id|Shintai|it|Shintai|ja|神体|jv|Shintai|ko|신체 (신토)|mk|Шинтаи|pl|Go-shintai|pt|Shintai|ru|Синтай (синтоизм)|simple|Shintai|sr|Шинтаи|tr|Shintai|uk|Сінтай (синто)|zh|神體|qid=Q327532}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. In the Jinmyōchō, many shrines list two seats with the pattern “place name + tsu + hiko/hime,” and in the case of Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine as well, it is considered appropriate to view the enshrined deities as the two local tutelary gods Sogatsuhiko and Sogatsuhime{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1982}}.
